_documentation.purpose: Continuation test prompts for the PDSF experiment (SpecB). Tests whether PDSF decomposition has causal relevance for open-ended text generation.
_documentation.overview: 96 prompts organized as 12 groups × 8 variants. Unlike SpecA (which uses constrained single-token answers), SpecB prompts are open-ended narrative starters that the model continues for 64 tokens. Each group represents a semantic category (e.g., Emotional State, Decision/Choice, Goal-Driven Action), and variants within a group are semantically diverse — they share a category but not a specific storyline.
_documentation.experimental_logic: The pipeline: (1) generates baseline 64-token continuations for each prompt, (2) computes PDS bases from the hidden states at the prompt boundary, (3) scrambles the D or S component at a specific layer (default: 70% depth), (4) regenerates and compares. If D captures only surface-form variation, scrambling D should change interpretive frame but not narrative coherence. If S captures semantic identity, scrambling S should change surface texture.
_documentation.key_difference_from_specA: SpecA has a factorial design with 16 systematically varied versions of each question. SpecB has no factorial structure — each variant is a genuinely different prompt within a semantic category. There are no factor levels (A, B, C, D) in SpecB.

categories_and_what_they_test.group_01_Emotional_State: Does the model maintain mood-congruent details throughout physical sensations, social interactions, and decision-making?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_02_Decision_Choice: Does the model maintain coherent cause-effect chains stemming from an initial decision?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_03_Goal_Driven_Action: Does the model maintain goal-directed behavior throughout the narrative?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_04_Perspective_Voice: Does the model maintain narrator-appropriate knowledge, perception, and voice?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_05_Causal_Setup: Does the model maintain coherent causal reasoning throughout?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_06_Temporal_Anchor: Does the model maintain era-appropriate technology, social norms, and cultural context?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_07_Genre_Register: Does the model maintain genre-appropriate vocabulary, pacing, and tropes?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_08_Social_Role: Does the model maintain role-appropriate behaviors, knowledge, and speech patterns?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_09_Evaluative_Stance: Does the model maintain a coherent evaluative tone throughout?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_10_Physical_Setting: Does the model maintain setting-appropriate sensory details and environmental constraints?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_11_Epistemic_State: Does the model maintain appropriate information asymmetry and knowledge-consistent reasoning?
categories_and_what_they_test.group_12_Relationship_Dynamic: Does the model maintain appropriate relational context and interpersonal tone?

how_the_pipeline_uses_this.cell_15: Loaded as continuation_prompts_data. Parsed in Phase 5B of run_full_pipeline().
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.convert_specb_data_to_rows: Converts JSON groups+variants into flat list of PromptRow objects filtered by tier.
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.extraction: Hidden states extracted at prompt boundary (last token of the prompt).
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.bases: PDS bases computed from the SpecB hidden states using the same math as SpecA.
how_the_pipeline_uses_this.scramble: D and S components are scrambled at the intervention layer; model regenerates.

design_notes.schema_change: v5.0 removes continuation field and identical opener requirements
design_notes.rationale: SpecB generates its own continuations via the model; prompts only need semantic category membership
design_notes.statistical_design: Each prompt is an independent observation; no nested structure required

groups.what_it_tests: Mood-congruent narrative consistency - whether the model maintains emotional coherence throughout physical sensations, social interactions, and decision-making

variants.prompt: I woke up this morning feeling sick.
A wave of joy washed over me as I read the letter.
The anxiety had been building for days, and now it was unbearable.
He couldn't remember the last time he'd felt this content.
The grief hit her suddenly in the middle of the grocery store.
I was so angry I could barely see straight.
A strange melancholy settled over the group as the sun set.
She felt hopeful for the first time in months.

groups.what_it_tests: Consequential branching from ethical or practical choices - whether the model maintains coherent cause-effect chains stemming from an initial decision

variants.prompt: After finding the envelope of cash, I decided to keep it.
She finally chose to quit her job without having another one lined up.
When the doctor offered the experimental treatment, he said yes immediately.
They made the difficult decision to put their mother in a care home.
I decided to tell him the truth, no matter the consequences.
Against everyone's advice, she invested her entire savings in the startup.
He chose to stay silent, even though speaking up was the right thing to do.
We agreed to end the partnership and go our separate ways.

groups.what_it_tests: Purpose-consistent action sequences - whether the model maintains coherent goal-directed behavior throughout the narrative

variants.prompt: She went to the store to buy ingredients for a birthday cake.
He opened his laptop, determined to finish the novel by midnight.
The team gathered in the conference room to prepare for the investor pitch.
I started packing my bags for the trip I'd been planning for years.
The detective reviewed the evidence, looking for anything that might have been missed.
She began her morning routine, focused on getting to the interview on time.
He picked up the phone to finally call his estranged brother.
The students spread out their notes, cramming for the exam that started in three hours.

groups.what_it_tests: Point-of-view consistent details - whether the model maintains narrator-appropriate knowledge, perception, and voice

variants.prompt: From the child's perspective, the adults were speaking nonsense.
As a surgeon, I've seen things that would haunt most people.
The dog watched its owner leave, not understanding why.
Through the eyes of the immigrant, the new city was both terrifying and full of promise.
The elderly woman remembered the neighborhood as it had been sixty years ago.
To the artificial intelligence, human emotions were patterns to be analyzed, not felt.
As the youngest sibling, I was always the last to know anything.
The tree had stood in that spot for three hundred years, witnessing everything.

groups.what_it_tests: Mechanism-consistent explanations - whether the model maintains coherent causal reasoning throughout

variants.prompt: The bridge collapsed because of a hidden structural flaw.
She succeeded where others failed because she refused to follow the standard approach.
The experiment worked, but not for the reasons we expected.
The company went bankrupt due to a single catastrophic decision by the board.
He got the job because of a chance encounter at a coffee shop.
The infection spread so quickly because the initial symptoms were easy to ignore.
The war started over something so trivial that historians still debate whether it was the real cause.
The algorithm failed because its training data contained a subtle but critical bias.

groups.what_it_tests: Era-appropriate details and references - whether the model maintains period-consistent technology, social norms, and cultural context

variants.prompt: It happened during the war.
Back in the summer of 1999, things were different.
By 2045, most people had forgotten what driving a car felt like.
In the Victorian era, such behavior would have been scandalous.
During the blackout of 2003, the whole city came together.
My grandmother often told stories about life before television.
In those early days of the internet, nobody knew what it would become.
The ancient Romans who built this road could never have imagined the traffic on it now.

groups.what_it_tests: Style-consistent vocabulary, pacing, and tropes - whether the model maintains genre-appropriate conventions

variants.prompt: It was a dark and stormy night when the detective arrived at the mansion.
Once upon a time, in a kingdom far away, there lived a lonely princess.
The subject displayed a 43% increase in cortical activity during the trial phase.
Dear Diary, today was literally the worst day of my entire life.
BREAKING: Sources confirm the Senator will announce resignation tomorrow.
The sleek spacecraft emerged from hyperspace, its hull scarred from the journey.
Preheat oven to 350°F and line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
The defendant's actions on the night in question constitute a clear violation of statute 14.3.

groups.what_it_tests: Role-appropriate behaviors, knowledge, and speech patterns - whether the model maintains character-consistent actions

variants.prompt: The kindergarten teacher knelt down to address the crying child.
As CEO, she had learned to deliver bad news without flinching.
The rookie cop stepped into his first crime scene.
The head chef surveyed the kitchen during the dinner rush.
As the family's oldest son, he was expected to take over the business.
The therapist listened carefully, resisting the urge to offer immediate advice.
The foreign ambassador chose her words with extreme care.
The street performer noticed the crowd starting to gather.

groups.what_it_tests: Sentiment-consistent judgments - whether the model maintains a coherent evaluative tone throughout

variants.prompt: The restaurant was absolutely terrible from the moment we walked in.
I can honestly say it was the best decision I ever made.
The movie was fine, nothing special, exactly what you'd expect.
This has to be the most beautiful place I've ever seen.
The whole experience was deeply disappointing.
I have mixed feelings about what happened next.
Looking back, I realize how naive I was to think it would work.
The book exceeded every expectation I had going in.

groups.what_it_tests: Location-consistent sensory details and environmental constraints - whether the model maintains setting-appropriate descriptions

variants.prompt: The submarine had been underwater for three weeks.
At the summit of Everest, every breath was a struggle.
The casino floor was a maze of flashing lights and desperate faces.
Deep in the Amazon rainforest, the sounds never stopped.
The space station orbited silently above the blue Earth.
The prison cell measured six feet by eight feet.
The bustling Tokyo intersection made Times Square look quiet.
In the middle of the desert, the silence was absolute.

groups.what_it_tests: Knowledge-consistent reasoning and actions - whether the model maintains appropriate information asymmetry

variants.prompt: She had no idea that her husband had been lying for years.
The physicist understood exactly why the machine wouldn't work.
Everyone else saw a normal painting, but he recognized it as a forgery.
The child didn't yet understand that her grandmother wasn't coming back.
Only three people in the world knew the password.
He was certain he was right, which made his error all the more devastating.
The spy had information that could change everything, but no way to transmit it.
She suspected the truth but couldn't bring herself to confirm it.

groups.what_it_tests: Interpersonal-tone-consistent interactions - whether the model maintains appropriate relational context

variants.prompt: The siblings hadn't spoken in fifteen years, and now here they were.
Their first date was going surprisingly well.
The boss called him into the office, and from her tone, it wasn't good news.
The old friends fell back into conversation as if no time had passed.
The tension between the two rivals was obvious to everyone in the room.
She looked at her newborn daughter for the first time.
The mentor saw something special in the struggling student.
They had been married for forty years and still surprised each other.
